candidates.why_relevant: Procedure for estimating numerical uncertainty from grid-refinement studies. Alternative, more robust refinement-based uncertainty estimation that could inform or sensitivity-test NeuroSem's tolerance constant c.

candidates.title: On Numerical Simulations of Integrate-and-Fire Neural Networks
candidates.authors: D. Hansel; G. Mato; C. Meunier; L. Neltner
candidates.found_via: Crossref query.bibliographic 'on numerical simulations of integrate-and-fire neural networks' (Crossref used because OpenAlex returned HTTP 429)
candidates.why_relevant: Retrieved abstract: very small time steps are needed with Euler or second-order Runge-Kutta to reproduce synchronization in integrate-and-fire networks, and an improved scheme is proposed. Neuroscience precedent that step size and solver choice silently change model behaviour, supporting NeuroSem's numerical mutation family and refinement-based tolerances.

candidates.title: Accuracy evaluation of numerical methods used in state-of-the-art simulators for spiking neural networks
candidates.authors: Stephan Henker; Johannes Partzsch; René Schüffny
candidates.found_via: Crossref query.bibliographic 'accuracy of spiking neuron simulators numerical integration comparison'
candidates.why_relevant: Journal of Computational Neuroscience paper evaluating the accuracy of numerical methods in widely used spiking-network simulators (title-level evidence; no abstract in Crossref). Classic integration-accuracy reference the critic flagged as missing; network simulators, no mutation or protocol selection.

candidates.title: How much can we trust neural simulation strategies?
candidates.authors: Michelle Rudolph; Alain Destexhe
candidates.found_via: Crossref query.bibliographic 'how much can we trust neural simulation strategies'
candidates.why_relevant: Neurocomputing paper (title-level evidence) questioning the reliability of neural simulation strategies. Supports treating numerical settings as a source of silent behavioural change in NeuroSem.

candidates.title: Exact Subthreshold Integration with Continuous Spike Times in Discrete-Time Neural Network Simulations
candidates.authors: Abigail Morrison; Sirko Straube; Hans Ekkehard Plesser; Markus Diesmann
candidates.found_via: Crossref query.bibliographic 'exact subthreshold integration with continuous spike times in discrete time neural network simulations'
candidates.why_relevant: Retrieved abstract: restricting spike times to the time grid loses accuracy with undesirable consequences, so continuous spike times are combined with exact subthreshold integration. Evidence that grid/time-step choices alter spike-timing features NeuroSem measures (latency, ISI).

candidates.title: Exact digital simulation of time-invariant linear systems with applications to neuronal modeling
candidates.authors: Stefan Rotter; Markus Diesmann
candidates.found_via: Crossref query.bibliographic 'exact digital simulation of time-invariant linear systems with applications to neuronal modeling'
candidates.why_relevant: Exact integration of linear neuronal dynamics (Biological Cybernetics). Background for the exact-integration option that makes step-size refinement trivial for some model classes; relevant when choosing NeuroSem fixtures and numerical mutants.

candidates.title: Efficient and Accurate Time-Stepping Schemes for Integrate-and-Fire Neuronal Networks
candidates.authors: Michael J. Shelley; Louis Tao
candidates.found_via: Crossref query.bibliographic 'efficient and accurate time-stepping schemes for integrate-and-fire neuronal networks'; also PubMed search (PMID 11717528)
candidates.why_relevant: PubMed abstract: addresses numerical errors from resetting the membrane potential after spikes in integrate-and-fire network simulations, via modified time stepping. Classic integration-accuracy reference for spike-reset models.

candidates.title: Spiking neural network simulation: numerical integration with the Parker-Sochacki method
candidates.authors: Robert D. Stewart; Wyeth Bair
candidates.found_via: Crossref query.bibliographic 'spiking neural network simulation numerical integration with the Parker-Sochacki method'; also PubMed search (PMID 19151930)
candidates.why_relevant: PubMed abstract: Parker-Sochacki integration for neuronal model ODEs with adaptive solution order. Relevant as a high-accuracy reference solver against which step-size tolerances could be checked.

candidates.title: Independent Variable Time-Step Integration of Individual Neurons for Network Simulations
candidates.authors: William W. Lytton; Michael L. Hines
candidates.found_via: Crossref query.bibliographic 'independent variable time-step integration of individual neurons for network simulations'
candidates.why_relevant: Retrieved abstract: local variable time-step integration (lvardt) for networks, per-neuron variable-step integrators in NEURON. Relevant because variable-step solver configuration is a candidate numerical mutation or valid-transformation family in NeuroSem.

candidates.title: Exact Simulation of Integrate-and-Fire Models with Synaptic Conductances
candidates.authors: Romain Brette
candidates.found_via: PubMed search '(numerical uncertainty OR solver accuracy OR time step) AND (neuroscience/neuron models OR Hodgkin-Huxley) AND journal filter' (PMID 16771661); DOI from PubMed metadata
candidates.why_relevant: PubMed abstract contrasts approximation methods with spike times binned to the time step against exact event-driven simulation of integrate-and-fire models with synaptic conductances. Supports the claim that simulation strategy is a behaviour-relevant setting.

candidates.title: The Backward Euler Method for Numerical Solution of the Hodgkin–Huxley Equations of Nerve Conduction
candidates.authors: Michael Mascagni
candidates.found_via: Crossref query.bibliographic 'numerical integration Hodgkin-Huxley equations stability accuracy'
candidates.why_relevant: Retrieved abstract: backward Euler method for the Hodgkin-Huxley cable PDEs. Classic numerical-analysis reference for conductance-based models, relevant to spatial and temporal discretization mutants.

candidates.title: On numerical integration of the Hodgkin and Huxley equations for a membrane action potential
candidates.authors: John W. Moore; Fidel Ramon
candidates.found_via: Crossref query.bibliographic 'numerical integration Hodgkin-Huxley equations stability accuracy'
candidates.why_relevant: Early paper on numerical integration of the Hodgkin-Huxley membrane action potential equations (title-level evidence). Historical integration-accuracy reference for conductance-based neuron models.

candidates.title: Automatically Selecting a Suitable Integration Scheme for Systems of Differential Equations in Neuron Models
candidates.authors: Inga Blundell; Dimitri Plotnikov; Jochen M. Eppler; Abigail Morrison
candidates.found_via: Crossref query.bibliographic 'automatically selecting a suitable integration scheme for systems of differential equations in neuron models'; first surfaced by Zenodo REST q='"stimulation protocol" selection neuron model'
candidates.why_relevant: Automatic selection of integration schemes for neuron-model ODEs (title-level evidence; no abstract in Crossref). Directly matches the critic's 'integration scheme selection neuron models' query; relevant to numerical-mutation design and to documenting solver choice per fixture.

candidates.title: ODE-toolbox: Automatic selection and generation of integration schemes for systems of ordinary differential equations
candidates.authors: Linssen, Charl; Jain, Shraddha; Morrison, Abigail; Eppler, Jochen Martin
candidates.found_via: Zenodo REST /api/communities/hbp/records q='validation OR validate OR testing OR test' (earlier version 10.5281/zenodo.3822082)
candidates.why_relevant: Zenodo record (license gpl-2.0 per record metadata): ODE-toolbox, a Python package for solver benchmarking and heuristic solver recommendation, generating exact propagators where possible. A reusable tool for checking whether NeuroSem's fixtures admit exact or reference solutions when calibrating tolerances.

candidates.title: Probabilistic solvers enable a straight-forward exploration of numerical uncertainty in neuroscience models
candidates.authors: Jonathan Oesterle; Nicholas Krämer; Philipp Hennig; Philipp Berens
candidates.found_via: Crossref abstract fetch after Europe PMC query '"integration method" AND ("spiking neuron" OR "Hodgkin-Huxley") AND (error OR accuracy)'; also PubMed (PMID 35932442)
candidates.why_relevant: Retrieved abstract: deterministic ODE solvers give single solutions without adequate error indication, so probabilistic solvers are used to explore numerical uncertainty in neuroscience models. Closest neuroscience alternative to NeuroSem's h, h/2, h/4 refinement tolerance rule; a candidate comparator or sensitivity analysis. No mutation testing or protocol selection.

candidates.title: Accuracy and Efficiency in Fixed-Point Neural ODE Solvers
candidates.authors: Michael Hopkins; Steve Furber
candidates.found_via: PubMed search with journal filter (PMID 26313605); DOI from PubMed metadata
candidates.why_relevant: PubMed abstract: accuracy versus efficiency of neural ODE solvers in fixed-point digital simulation. Shows that numeric representation and solver affect neural behaviour, relevant to numeric-formatting valid transformations and numerical mutants.

candidates.title: Structural Fuzzing: Adapting Input Mutation Testing for Parameterized Model Validation
candidates.authors: Bond, Andrew H.
candidates.found_via: DataCite query titles.title:("mutation testing") AND descriptions.description:(simulation OR scientific); Zenodo record fetched
